title: Names, let, and const

blocks.md:
## A name is a box

`let` names a box you can refill. `const` names a box you cannot *rebind* — the sticker on the box stays. If the value is an object, the stuff *inside* can still change.

On the desk: `const signal = { on: false }; signal.on = true` is legal. `signal = {}` is not. The name still points at the same record. The lamp field flipped.

blocks.promptMd: After `const route = { dir: "east" }; route.dir = "south"`, what is `route.dir`?

choices.md: `"south"` — the binding stayed, the field changed

blocks.promptMd: `const` stops you from changing a field on an object.
blocks.explainMd: const stops a new assignment to that name. Fields on the object can still change.

blocks.promptMd: > `labelBox` should return the string `locked` from a `const` binding. Print that word.

hintLadder.md: const names a binding. You can still read it.

description: A name is a box for a value. Some boxes you can refill. Some you cannot rebind.
